prologue.text:
The Long Map wakes before the convoy does.

Not literally. It is not an intelligence, no matter what children whisper in the sleep decks. It is an archive, a routing lattice, a weather report for folded space, a family ledger with better math. It is ink, light, stone, algorithm, superstition, and every nervous correction a Vale has made in the margins for one hundred and forty years.

Tonight, it waits for another hand.

Your hand.

choices.label: Open the first survey record.
Read the official summary first.

prologue.scene: The Long Map Archive — Index Chamber

insets.text: LATTICE CONVOY ARCHIVAL INTERFACE  —  FAMILY ACCESS: VALE

overlays.text: Every route begins as an argument someone survived.

official_summary.text:
The official summary is clean, which means someone has polished it.

It says the Vale Line discovered the Esho Current during a routine survey. It says the route stabilized trade, reduced slipfold fuel expenditure by twelve percent, and became a defining achievement of convoy navigation.

It does not mention the argument in the dome.

It does not mention the beacon that failed thirty-two years later.

It does not mention what the third generation found written underneath the first map.

choices.label: Open the first survey record.

insets.text: OFFICIAL SUMMARY  —  EDUCATIONAL EDITION  —  REVISION 18

overlays.text: Clean histories are usually maintained, not discovered.

g1_dome.text:
Elian Vale is seventeen when the stars first look close enough to touch.

The observation dome of the survey cutter Iris Bell is barely wider than a cargo lift, but the transparent hull makes it feel like standing inside a held breath. Ahead, the Esho region bends the field readings into impossible ribbons. Behind, the Lattice Convoy glows in orderly formation: school ship, hydroponics barge, fabrication spine, hospital tender, chapel observatory, and the thousand warm windows of people who will never know your name if you do your job correctly.

Your mother, Captain Sera Vale, rests one hand on the rail.

"Your first independent correction," she says. "Show me the current."

choices.label: Trust the instruments and mark the current as viable.
Ask for another pass before making the mark.
Admit the readings scare you.

g1_dome.scene: GENERATION ONE — Iris Bell, Observation Dome

insets.text: SURVEY CUTTER IRIS BELL  —  OUTER ESHO REGION  —  03:12 CONVOY STANDARD

overlays.text: The dome glass creaks with thermal settling. Your mother pretends not to hear it.

g1_mark_viable.text:
You mark the current as viable.

The line appears on the dome display: a thin cyan thread through a region the older maps leave blank. It feels too easy. The Long Map accepts the notation without ceremony.

Your mother studies it for long enough that your stomach tightens.

"Bold," she says. Not praise. Not criticism. A coordinate held in suspension.

choices.label: Defend the mark with the data.
Add a caution annotation before anyone can object.

insets.text: LONG MAP TEMPORARY MARKER  —  ESHO-CANDIDATE-1  —  STATUS: UNCONFIRMED

overlays.text: Bold becomes brave only if the math survives.

g1_request_pass.text:
"Good," your mother says before you can explain yourself.

She orders the Iris Bell into a second pass. The cutter rolls, and the folded light ahead rearranges itself like cloth tugged from underneath a table. On the second scan, a resonance spike appears where your first sweep showed open passage.

Not a wall.

A warning.

choices.label: Annotate the spike as a manageable hazard.
Recommend abandoning the candidate route.

overlays.text: The second look is why the Vale Line has survived this long.

g1_admit_fear.text:
"It scares me," you say.

Your mother does not smile. She does not soften. That would make the lesson smaller.

"It should," she says. "If folded space ever stops scaring you, hand the chart to someone less impressed with themselves."

She turns the display toward you again.

"Now tell me whether fear sees anything the instruments missed."

choices.label: Use the fear. Request another pass.
Separate fear from evidence and mark the current.

overlays.text: Fear is not a conclusion. Sometimes it is a sensor.

g1_abandon_candidate.text:
You recommend abandoning the candidate route.

For a moment, the bridge is silent except for the soft tick of rangefinder relays. Then your mother asks the question every Vale learns to dread.

"Are you protecting the convoy," she says, "or protecting yourself from being wrong?"

The answer matters less than the fact that you do not have one ready.

choices.label: Concede a limited probe could still be justified.
Stand by the recommendation.

g1_abandon_candidate.scene: GENERATION ONE — Iris Bell, Survey Bridge

insets.text: BRIDGE LOG  —  ROUTE CANDIDATE FLAGGED FOR CAPTAIN REVIEW

g1_survey_bridge.text:
On the survey bridge, the rest of the crew gathers around your candidate line.

People do not crowd in the Lattice Convoy. Crowding implies panic. Instead they arrange themselves in respectful arcs, each person with enough room to pretend the decision is only technical.

Navigator Osei taps the fuel projection. "If this current holds, we shave nineteen days off the Mirrorglass leg."

"Or lose a cutter proving it does not," Chief Engineer Pan replies.

Your mother looks at you.

"The map is listening."

choices.label: Argue for a controlled probe.
Argue that the convoy should wait for more data.
Ask the crew what risks they see before speaking.

g1_survey_bridge.scene: GENERATION ONE — Iris Bell, Survey Bridge

insets.text: PROJECTED BENEFIT: -19 DAYS  —  PROJECTED RISK: UNMODELED RESONANCE

overlays.text: A map is a promise made before the road exists.

g1_crew_input.text:
You ask the crew what risks they see.

That earns you three immediate arguments, one muttered blessing from the comms officer, and a look from your mother that may become pride later if everyone survives.

The bridge becomes what the convoy is at its best: not agreement, but disciplined disagreement with shared oxygen.

choices.label: Shape their concerns into a probe plan.
Shape their concerns into a delay recommendation.

overlays.text: The Long Map was never written by one hand, no matter whose family name is on the spine.

g1_probe_launch.text:
The probe is no larger than a coffin and much more expensive.

It launches from the Iris Bell with a polite mechanical shudder, vanishes into the candidate current, and returns twelve seconds before the model predicts it should.

Twelve seconds early.

The bridge goes very quiet.

choices.label: Treat the time gain as a breakthrough.
Treat the time gain as a hazard.
Say nothing until the telemetry is decoded.

g1_probe_launch.scene: GENERATION ONE — Iris Bell, Probe Control

insets.text: PROBE RETURN DELTA: -00:00:12.4  —  CAUSAL INTEGRITY: ACCEPTABLE

g1_probe_breakthrough.text:
"Nineteen days and twelve seconds," Osei whispers, already doing the math.

Your chest fills before you can stop it. There is a particular intoxication in discovering that the universe has been wasting your time and you can prove it.

Your mother cuts through the room.

"No one celebrates until we know what it cost."

choices.label: Volunteer to review the telemetry yourself.
Let Osei lead the review and observe.

overlays.text: Discovery has a taste. Metal, sugar, danger.

g1_probe_hazard.text:
"Time gain is not free," you say.

The words land badly. No one wants the first miracle of the week to arrive with an invoice.

Chief Pan nods anyway. "Kid is right. Fold currents do not give gifts. They make trades."

Your mother logs your objection in the route record.

choices.label: Volunteer to find the trade.
Recommend the candidate remain restricted.

insets.text: ANNOTATION ADDED: TEMPORAL GAIN REQUIRES COST MODEL

g1_decode_silence.text:
You say nothing.

The data decodes in layered bands: radiation, shear, drift, harmonic compression, fuel estimates, return stability. Every number seems survivable by itself. Together they form a sentence no one can quite read.

Your mother finally speaks.

"Bring it to the Assembly Ring."

choices.label: Prepare a cautious presentation.
Prepare an ambitious presentation.

overlays.text: Silence is sometimes mistaken for wisdom. Sometimes it is only silence.

g1_decode_telemetry.text:
The telemetry is beautiful in the way dangerous things often are.

The Esho Current is real. It does not violate the convoy's models; it embarrasses them. With careful calibration, the Lattice could cross the Mirrorglass leg in nineteen fewer days, maybe twenty-two in favorable mass distribution.

There is one instability: a resonance pocket that pulses every eleven years.

Small. Predictable. Easy to annotate.

Easy to underestimate.

choices.label: Recommend formal adoption with a warning marker.
Recommend limited use by survey craft only.
Recommend immediate convoy adoption.

insets.text: LONG MAP CANDIDATE: ESHO CURRENT  —  BENEFIT: HIGH  —  PERIODIC RESONANCE: 11.3 YEARS

g1_route_debate.text:
The Assembly Ring is built in the oldest vessel of the convoy, a round chamber with the first generation's handprints sealed beneath the floor glass.

Representatives speak in turn. Agriculture wants shorter routes before the next seedbank rotation. Education wants delay until the children finish their transit year. Fabrication wants salvage rights along the new current. Medical asks how many ships would be exposed if your annotation is wrong.

Then they call the Vale Line.

Your mother does not stand.

You do.

choices.label: Present the Esho Current as a careful opportunity.
Present it as the future of the convoy.
Present it as too dangerous for civilian use.

g1_route_debate.scene: GENERATION ONE — Assembly Ring, Founders Vessel

insets.text: ASSEMBLY MOTION  —  WHETHER TO AUTHORIZE ESHO CURRENT AS CONVOY ROUTE

overlays.text: Your voice sounds younger in public.

g1_vote.text:
The vote is not unanimous. Important things rarely are.

But the Esho Current enters the Long Map.

Not as certainty. Not as destiny. As a route with conditions, warnings, and your first permanent annotation. Your mother signs beneath it. Then she offers you the stylus.

"Do not write like you are finishing something," she says. "Write like someone will need to correct you."

choices.label: Write a humble annotation.
Write a proud annotation.
Write a warning so strong no one can ignore it.

insets.text: MOTION PASSED  —  ROUTE STATUS: PROVISIONAL CIVILIAN USE

overlays.text: A provisional route is still a route. People will build habits on it by breakfast.

g1_first_annotation.text:
You add the annotation.

Your handwriting looks absurdly human inside the Long Map: a slight upward lean, a pressure mark where the stylus catches, a correction squeezed into the margin because you misjudged the space.

No ceremony follows. The convoy does not know history has happened yet.

It only knows tomorrow's route is shorter.

choices.label: Close Elian's record.

g1_first_annotation.scene: GENERATION ONE — Long Map Archive, Annotation Desk

insets.text: ANNOTATION ACCEPTED  —  AUTHOR: E. VALE  —  STATUS: ACTIVE

overlays.text: Every tradition begins as someone's handwriting.

interlude_1.text:
For twenty-six years, the Esho Current behaves.

Children are born who have never known the old Mirrorglass leg. A bakery on the agriculture barge names a pastry after the twelve-second probe. Pilots joke that the Vale Line found a shortcut through impatience itself.

Then a relay beacon near the resonance pocket misses its maintenance window.

Not by much.

Enough.

choices.label: Open Generation Two.

insets.text: ROUTE USAGE: 9,204 TRANSITS  —  FATAL INCIDENTS: 0  —  DEFERRED MAINTENANCE EVENTS: 1

overlays.text: Safe routes become invisible. Invisible things are easiest to neglect.

g2_mara_intro.text:
Mara Vale has heard her father's annotation recited by schoolchildren, misquoted by councilors, and printed on mugs.

She has also spent three days listening to captains blame him for a failed beacon he warned them to maintain.

The Assembly Ring is louder now than in Elian's recording. More ships, more dependents, more schedules built on the assumption that Esho will hold because it always has.

At the center of the chamber, the damaged beacon's memory core waits in a sealed case.

choices.label: Read Elian's original warning aloud.
Focus on repairing the route, not defending the family.
Demand to know who deferred maintenance.

g2_mara_intro.scene: GENERATION TWO — Assembly Ring, Crisis Session

insets.text: BEACON E-17 FAILURE  —  DELAYED MAINTENANCE: 43 DAYS  —  TRAFFIC IMPACT: SEVERE

overlays.text: Your father wrote like someone would need to correct him. They turned the correction into a slogan.
Your father's proudest line is being used by people who did not read the sentence after it.
Your father's warning was strong enough to remember, but not strong enough to fund.

g2_read_warning.text:
You request the original record.

The chamber dims while the Long Map projects Elian Vale's annotation, unpolished and unhelpfully precise. The part everyone quotes is there. So is the part they omit: the eleven-year resonance warning, the maintenance condition, the recommendation against political normalization.

Silence spreads.

Not shame. Not yet.

Recognition.

choices.label: Use the silence to argue for route restrictions.
Use the silence to argue for better maintenance funding.

insets.text: ORIGINAL ANNOTATION RECOVERED  —  PUBLIC EDUCATION EXCERPT FOUND INCOMPLETE

overlays.text: Truth does not become useful just because it has been recovered.

g2_repair_focus.text:
You refuse to let the room turn your father into either a saint or a scapegoat.

"The beacon failed," you say. "The current did not. If we make this a memorial argument, the next ship enters Esho blind."

It is not the most poetic thing a Vale has ever said.

It is the thing the room needed.

choices.label: Authorize emergency repairs and temporary convoy slowdown.
Authorize repairs without slowing the convoy.

overlays.text: Sometimes legacy is a distraction from the broken part in front of you.

g2_accountability.text:
"Who deferred maintenance?" you ask.

The logistics representative flinches. The agriculture delegate looks at the floor. Education whispers with medical. Everyone knows the answer is not one person.

Forty-three days were shaved away in increments: seed priority, medicine priority, fuel priority, school transfer priority. Each delay was reasonable. Together they became failure.

choices.label: Name the system, not the scapegoat.
Force a public accountability vote.

overlays.text: Civilization rarely fails all at once. It signs small extensions.

g2_system_blame.text:
You refuse the easy execution.

"This is a route governance failure," you say. "If we punish one clerk, we teach the next clerk to hide the next delay."

The room dislikes this because it offers work instead of relief.

The damaged beacon core clicks softly in its case, cooling under legal custody.

choices.label: Propose a permanent Route Stewardship Office.
Propose rotating civilian oversight.

insets.text: PROPOSED CLASSIFICATION: ROUTE GOVERNANCE FAILURE

g2_accountability_vote.text:
You force the vote.

It feels good for approximately six minutes.

A logistics administrator loses her post. The chamber exhales. The convoy receives a clean story: one failure, one responsible name, one corrective action.

The beacon remains broken.

choices.label: Push past the scapegoat and still fund repairs.
Accept the vote and focus on immediate repair.

overlays.text: A clean story is not the same as a repaired route.

g2_restriction_motion.text:
You propose restricting Esho traffic until the resonance pocket is fully resurveyed.

The room reacts as if you have suggested turning off gravity for moral clarity.

Esho is not just a route anymore. It is medicine schedules, apprenticeship rotations, trade calendars, courtship visits, engine part deliveries, and the promise that the convoy is still moving forward.

To restrict it is to touch everyone.

choices.label: Accept the economic pain and restrict the route.
Compromise: restrict heavy vessels only.
Withdraw and pursue maintenance funding instead.

insets.text: ESTIMATED IMPACT OF FULL RESTRICTION: 31% DELAY ACROSS CONVOY SYSTEMS

g2_funding_motion.text:
You ask for boring money.

Beacon maintenance. Route auditors. Survey apprenticeships. Redundant markers. A review schedule that cannot be deferred by any single department without public notation.

No one applauds.

That is how you know the proposal might actually matter.

choices.label: Tie funding to public transparency.
Tie funding to navigator authority.
Keep the proposal narrow so it passes.

insets.text: MOTION: ROUTE STEWARDSHIP FUND  —  STATUS: DEBATE OPEN

g2_civilian_oversight.text:
You propose letting civilians see the maintenance schedule.

The navigators hate it. Logistics hates it. The Assembly hates the idea that everyone in the convoy might suddenly develop opinions about orbital markers and resonance drift.

Which means the proposal has teeth.

choices.label: Attach oversight to the funding motion.
Save oversight for later and secure repairs now.

overlays.text: Maps are public when they inspire confidence, private when they explain blame.

g2_restriction_passes.text:
The restriction passes by three votes.

The convoy slows.

Within hours, the complaint nets fill with messages: delayed insulin, missed apprenticeship exams, old relatives who cannot make the memorial transfer, a wedding postponed past the bride's deployment window.

You were right.

That does not make anyone grateful.

choices.label: Visit the damaged beacon yourself.

insets.text: ROUTE STATUS: RESTRICTED  —  PUBLIC APPROVAL: LOW  —  SAFETY MARGIN: IMPROVED

overlays.text: Correct decisions can still hurt people by name.

g2_heavy_restrict.text:
The compromise passes.

Heavy ships must divert. Light craft may continue under advisory. It is messy, uneven, politically survivable, and scientifically imperfect.

In other words, governance.

choices.label: Visit the damaged beacon yourself.

insets.text: ROUTE STATUS: PARTIAL RESTRICTION  —  RISK REDUCED, NOT REMOVED

g2_repair_mission.text:
The beacon hangs in the dark like a small, embarrassed moon.

Up close, the failure is not dramatic. A micrometeor scar. A thermal hinge stuck half-open. A calibration packet deferred so often the local software began trusting its own drift.

Your repair skiff clamps to the service ring. Inside your helmet, your father's old annotation scrolls beside the live telemetry.

He was right.

He was also incomplete.

choices.label: Repair the beacon exactly to Elian's specification.
Update the specification based on twenty-six years of route data.
Add an emergency warning marker stronger than the data requires.

g2_repair_mission.scene: GENERATION TWO — Beacon E-17, Service Ring

insets.text: BEACON E-17  —  ACCESS PANEL OPEN  —  LOCAL CLOCK DRIFT: 00:04:31

overlays.text: The old map got you here. It cannot do the repair for you.

g2_exact_repair.text:
You restore the beacon exactly as your father specified.

There is comfort in obedience to the dead. The light returns. The route marker stabilizes. The skiff fills with the clean ping of a system becoming itself again.

But the current has shifted since Elian wrote his warning.

Not much.

Enough.

choices.label: Record the repair as faithful restoration.

overlays.text: Sometimes reverence is a slower kind of error.

g2_updated_repair.text:
You update the specification.

For a moment, your glove hovers over the authorization control. Changing Elian Vale's original route architecture feels like correcting scripture with a wrench.

Then you remember he told you, again and again, that the map was not a shrine.

You authorize the update.

choices.label: Record the repair as a living revision.

insets.text: SPECIFICATION UPDATED  —  AUTHOR: M. VALE  —  REASON: CURRENT DRIFT

overlays.text: Your father would have argued with you. Then he would have checked the math.

g2_overwarning.text:
You add a stronger warning than the data requires.

The beacon now flashes amber at thresholds most pilots would consider acceptable. It will slow traffic. It will annoy captains. It will create meetings.

It will also be very hard to ignore.

choices.label: Record the warning as necessary caution.

insets.text: WARNING THRESHOLD MODIFIED  —  CAUTION BAND EXPANDED

g2_after_repair.text:
When the beacon comes back online, the convoy's route display blooms with light.

For three seconds, every ship sees the same thing: the old route, corrected by a living hand.

Then the system compresses the update into a neat public notice.

MAINTENANCE COMPLETE.

It feels insulting.

It is also true.

choices.label: Add a personal note to the Long Map.
Keep the record strictly technical.

insets.text: BEACON E-17  —  STATUS: OPERATIONAL  —  PUBLIC NOTICE ISSUED

overlays.text: The convoy will remember this as a maintenance event. Your hands will not.

g2_personal_note.text:
You add a personal note in a field usually reserved for calibration commentary.

It says: The route is not the inheritance. The responsibility is.

You almost delete it.

You do not.

choices.label: Close Mara's record.

g2_personal_note.scene: GENERATION TWO — Long Map Archive, Revision Desk

insets.text: ANNOTATION ACCEPTED  —  AUTHOR: M. VALE  —  VISIBILITY: TECHNICAL ARCHIVE

overlays.text: A sentence can sleep for decades before becoming dangerous.

g2_technical_note.text:
You keep the record technical.

Drift value. Calibration packet. Updated maintenance interval. Beacon response curve. No metaphor. No family defense. No sentence future students can carve into ceremony.

It is clean work.

You are not sure whether that makes it honest or lonely.

choices.label: Close Mara's record.

g2_technical_note.scene: GENERATION TWO — Long Map Archive, Revision Desk

insets.text: ANNOTATION ACCEPTED  —  AUTHOR: M. VALE  —  VISIBILITY: TECHNICAL ARCHIVE

overlays.text: Not every truth needs to become a saying.

interlude_2.text:
Decades pass in the way they do aboard moving civilizations: one maintenance cycle, one school term, one harvest, one funeral, one new window cut into an old ship.

The Esho Current remains open.

The story changes.

Elian becomes the discoverer. Mara becomes either the dutiful restorer, the necessary reformer, or the woman who slowed the convoy, depending on who is speaking and what they need the past to prove.

By the time Tovin Vale enters the archive, the route is no longer just a route.

It is curriculum.

choices.label: Open Generation Three.

insets.text: EDUCATIONAL MODULE: THE ESHO LEGACY  —  APPROVED FOR CIVIC YEAR STUDENTS
COMMON SAYING RECORDED: The route is not the inheritance. The responsibility is.

overlays.text: Memory does not preserve the past. It negotiates with it.

g3_tovin_class.text:
Tovin Vale is old enough to know when a lesson has been sanded smooth.

The civic year students sit in the observation tier while the instructor projects the Esho Current in ceremonial blue. Elian's first annotation appears as a heroic quote. Mara's repair appears as a moral example. The convoy appears, as it always does in school modules, wiser than any one person and less frightened than everyone actually was.

A child raises her hand.

"Did they know it would work?"

The instructor smiles.

Tovin looks at the archive access key warm in their palm.

choices.label: Let the simplified lesson stand.
Ask the instructor to show the original records.
Say nothing now. Pull the records yourself later.

g3_tovin_class.scene: GENERATION THREE — Education Ship Orison, Observation Tier

insets.text: CIVIC MODULE 12: ESHO CURRENT  —  LESSON TITLE: COURAGE IN CARTOGRAPHY

overlays.text: The heroic version of your family has better posture than anyone you have met.
The sentence survived. You wonder what it cost to become beautiful.

g3_after_class.text:
You let the lesson stand.

The children leave with bright eyes and a clean story. There is value in that. A civilization cannot feed its young only ambiguity and maintenance reports.

Still, when the room empties, the projected route remains hovering above the seats.

It looks less like a road than a question someone taught everyone to answer too quickly.

choices.label: Go to the Long Map Archive.

overlays.text: A myth can be false in detail and useful in weather.

g3_challenge_lesson.text:
"Show them the original," you say.

The instructor's smile holds, then tightens. The children turn toward you with the immediate hunger of people sensing adult discomfort.

"We simplify for civic comprehension," the instructor says.

"Then say that," you reply. "Simplification is not the same as truth."

choices.label: Apologize and request private archive access.
Push harder in front of the class.

overlays.text: The first crack in a polished story sounds rude.

g3_public_dispute.text:
You push harder.

It becomes a scene, which is exactly what the education officers will call it later. A Vale disrupting a civic lesson. A young archivist embarrassing an instructor. A family heir mistaking complexity for wisdom.

The students love it.

That may be the problem.

choices.label: Accept formal censure and continue privately.

insets.text: EDUCATION OFFICE NOTICE  —  UNAPPROVED HISTORICAL COMPLICATION DURING CIVIC MODULE

g3_archive_theft.text:
You wait until the lesson ends.

The archive key was your grandmother's. Officially, it grants family annotation rights. Unofficially, it opens rooms the education module does not admit exist.

The Long Map Archive recognizes your palm with a soft tone.

WELCOME, T. VALE.

The door opens like it has been expecting you.

choices.label: Enter the restricted record chain.

g3_archive_theft.scene: GENERATION THREE — Long Map Archive, Restricted Stack

insets.text: FAMILY ACCESS ACCEPTED  —  RESTRICTED ESHO CHAIN AVAILABLE

overlays.text: Some doors are locked to keep secrets in. Some are locked to make opening them feel like choice.

g3_archive_entry.text:
The restricted stack smells faintly of coolant and old cloth.

Every generation thinks archives will feel clean because records are supposed to settle things. They never do. The oldest storage shelves are patched with three fabrication standards. The touchscreen nearest the Esho chain has a handwritten label: PRESS GENTLY OR IT LIES.

You open the original sequence.

Elian's voice fills the room, young and uncertain.

Then Mara's, older and tired.

Then a file you have never seen before.

choices.label: Play Elian's unedited survey record.
Play Mara's beacon revision record.
Open the unknown file.

insets.text: RESTRICTED CHAIN: ESHO CURRENT  —  ITEMS: 3 STANDARD, 1 SEALED

overlays.text: The past is much less composed when it does not know it is being quoted.

g3_elian_record.text:
Elian's record is not heroic.

It is full of pauses, corrections, requests for second scans, and one whispered curse when the probe returns early. He sounds brilliant, yes. He also sounds seventeen.

Near the end, your great-grandfather says: "Do not let them name it after me. Routes belong to the people who maintain them."

The school module cut that part.

choices.label: Mark the omission for public correction.
Keep listening before deciding what to do.

overlays.text: The discoverer did not want a monument.
If your first annotation was humble, the omission feels almost violent.

g3_mara_record.text:
Mara's beacon record is worse than the lesson.

Not morally. Emotionally.

She is outside Beacon E-17, breathing hard, arguing with three departments on a shared channel while recalibrating a hinge with one hand. Her voice breaks only once, when someone calls her father's warning symbolic.

"It was a maintenance condition," she snaps. "Symbols do not keep ships alive."

choices.label: Mark Mara's technical correction as central history.
Keep listening before deciding what to do.

overlays.text: The route is not the inheritance. The responsibility is.
A clean record can still sound lonely.

g3_unknown_file.text:
The unknown file opens without title.

It is an Assembly private session, recorded two weeks after the beacon repair. Representatives debate whether to preserve the messy version of events or simplify it for civic education.

One voice says, "Children need exemplars."

Another says, "Navigators need warnings."

A third says, "The convoy needs both and has time for neither."

Then comes the vote.

choices.label: Watch the vote.
Stop the file and breathe for a moment.

insets.text: SEALED FILE  —  ASSEMBLY EDUCATION SUBCOMMITTEE  —  ACCESS LOG INCOMPLETE

overlays.text: Not all censorship hates truth. Some of it loves usefulness more.

g3_breathe_archive.text:
You stop the file.

In the silence, the archive hum feels almost kind. Beyond the wall, the convoy continues its ordinary evening: dinner rotations, shift changes, students complaining about assignments, old couples walking the inner ring for circulation.

All of them live inside stories they did not personally verify.

So do you.

choices.label: Resume the sealed file.
Open all records side by side.

overlays.text: No one can fact-check a civilization before breakfast.

g3_vote_file.text:
The vote passes.

The education module will simplify the Esho history. Elian becomes courage. Mara becomes responsibility. The maintenance failure becomes an example, not an indictment. The route remains a shared accomplishment, stripped of enough argument to fit inside a child's morning.

Then the recording captures Mara speaking from the back of the room.

"If you simplify it," she says, "leave a door back to the whole version."

choices.label: Search for the door Mara left.
Decide the simplified version may have been necessary.

insets.text: VOTE RESULT: CIVIC SIMPLIFICATION APPROVED  —  MINORITY CONDITION ACCEPTED

overlays.text: A compromise can be cowardice, wisdom, or both. History rarely labels which.

g3_mara_door.text:
You search the archive index for Mara's condition.

There it is: a narrow retrieval path hidden behind three harmless lesson references, a maintenance footnote, and a quote children memorize without understanding.

The door was never locked.

It was disguised as homework.

choices.label: Follow the hidden retrieval path.

insets.text: RETRIEVAL PATH FOUND  —  PUBLIC ACCESS POSSIBLE THROUGH CIVIC MODULE FOOTNOTES

overlays.text: Your grandmother did not save the truth by winning. She saved it by making it findable.

g3_accept_simplification.text:
You sit with the unpleasant possibility that the simplified lesson was not simply a lie.

Children need beginnings. Convoys need shared language. No one can inherit every argument raw.

But if simplification becomes the only door, memory turns into a corridor with no rooms.

choices.label: Look for whether Mara left another door.
Prepare to defend the existing lesson.

overlays.text: A story can shelter people. It can also trap them.

g3_records_compare.text:
You arrange the records side by side.

Elian's uncertainty. Mara's exhaustion. The Assembly's compromise. The children's lesson. The public route map. The private maintenance chain. The family notes. The jokes. The mugs. The memorial plaque. The arguments.

None of them alone are the truth.

Together, they are inconvenient enough to resemble it.

choices.label: Prepare a public correction.
Prepare a layered archive release for students.
Prepare a defense of the existing myth.

g3_records_compare.scene: GENERATION THREE — Long Map Archive, Comparison Table

insets.text: RECORDS ALIGNED  —  CONTRADICTIONS: 14  —  IRRECONCILABLE: 0
FAMILY ANNOTATION THREAD COMPLETE

overlays.text: Complexity is not the enemy of memory. It is the cost of keeping adults in the room.

g3_public_correction.text:
You draft the correction in direct language.

The Esho story taught in civic modules is incomplete. The route was adopted under uncertainty. The maintenance failure was systemic. The heroic version omits conditions essential to convoy safety.

It is accurate.

It is also a thrown tool in a crowded engine room.

choices.label: Publish it openly before the council can soften it.
Bring it to the council first.

overlays.text: Truth delivered without timing becomes weather.

g3_layered_release.text:
You design the release as a map, not a verdict.

Children can keep the simple story. Apprentices can open the caution layer. Navigators can access the full maintenance chain. Citizens can trace every quote back to its source if they choose.

Not everyone will.

But the door will be visible.

choices.label: Bring the layered release to the council.
Publish the layered archive quietly through the education module.

insets.text: PROPOSED CIVIC MODULE REVISION  —  SURFACE STORY + ACCESSIBLE DEPTH LAYERS

overlays.text: A good map does not force every traveler down every road.

g3_publish_open.text:
You publish the correction.

For six minutes, nothing happens.

Then everything does.

Students share clips. Navigators argue in public. Education officers accuse you of context collapse. Logistics asks why maintenance deferral records are suddenly trending. The Assembly schedules an emergency session using language normally reserved for hull breaches and wedding disputes.

choices.label: Face the emergency session.

insets.text: PUBLIC NETWORK STATUS  —  ESHO THREAD TRENDING ACROSS 19 VESSELS

overlays.text: The convoy is not angry because you lied. It is angry because you made everyone update at once.

g3_quiet_release.text:
You publish the layered archive quietly.

No announcement. No accusation. No grand correction.

Just a new link in the civic module: SEE SOURCE CHAIN.

At first, almost no one clicks it.

Then one student does. Then a navigation apprentice. Then an old maintenance clerk who remembers Beacon E-17 and sends a message containing only: thank you.

choices.label: Prepare for the council review that will inevitably follow.

insets.text: CIVIC MODULE UPDATED  —  SOURCE CHAIN LINK ADDED

overlays.text: Some revolutions begin as better footnotes.

g3_council_call.text:
The Assembly Ring has changed again.

New glass over old handprints. New representatives under old procedural lights. The Esho route hangs above the chamber in three layers: public story, technical record, family annotation chain.

They ask you what you want.

It is the wrong question.

The better question is what the convoy should be allowed to inherit.

choices.label: Argue for preserving the simple civic myth.
Argue for public correction, even if unity suffers.
Argue that the convoy must leave Esho behind.
Argue for a layered map: story, source, and correction together.
Seal the restricted archive and protect social cohesion.

g3_council_call.scene: GENERATION THREE — Assembly Ring, Esho Review

insets.text: ASSEMBLY MOTION  —  CIVIC STATUS OF ESHO CURRENT HISTORY

overlays.text: Elian discovered a route. Mara kept it honest enough to survive. You are deciding whether honesty can be inherited.
The simple story is wounded, but not dead.
A quiet door is open. The question is whether to put a sign above it.

ending_stable_route.text:
The Assembly preserves the civic story.

Not unchanged. That would be too crude. A new appendix is added for advanced students. A maintenance note is restored. Mara's hidden retrieval path remains technically available.

But the lesson stays simple.

Elian discovered. Mara preserved. The convoy continued.

Years later, children still recite the route story in the observation tier. Some of them grow curious enough to open the deeper records. Most do not.

The Esho Current remains stable.

So does the myth.

insets.text: CIVIC MODULE STATUS: REVISED LIGHTLY  —  PUBLIC UNITY: HIGH  —  HISTORICAL NUANCE: LIMITED

overlays.text: A civilization can survive on simplified truth. The question is what kind of adults it produces.

ending_revision.text:
The correction passes.

Not cleanly. Nothing important does.

For months, the convoy argues about the Esho Current with the ferocity of people discovering their childhood had footnotes. Elian becomes less heroic and more human. Mara becomes less symbolic and more difficult. The Assembly's old compromise becomes a case study in civic ethics.

Unity weakens.

Safety improves.

Years later, the children still learn the Esho story. Now the first question in the module is not Who found the route?

It is: What did they not know yet?

insets.text: CIVIC MODULE STATUS: FULLY REVISED  —  PUBLIC UNITY: STRESSED  —  ROUTE LITERACY: IMPROVED

overlays.text: Truth did not heal the convoy. It gave the convoy better pain.

ending_new_current.text:
You argue that no story, however well repaired, can substitute for movement.

The convoy begins a ten-year transition away from permanent Esho dependence. It hurts. Settlements along the route renegotiate supply calendars. Some families accuse the Vale Line of abandoning its own legacy. Others volunteer for new survey crews before the vote is even finished.

The Long Map opens a new section.

Blank.

Terrifying.

Merciful.

insets.text: ROUTE STRATEGY: DIVERSIFICATION APPROVED  —  ESHO DEPENDENCY REDUCTION: 10-YEAR PLAN

overlays.text: Sometimes honoring a route means refusing to be trapped by it.

ending_lantern_path.text:
The Assembly accepts the layered map.

The children keep the story, but every quote now glows with a source marker. Apprentices can open Elian's uncertainty. Citizens can hear Mara's repair log. The maintenance schedule is public. The old simplified lesson remains as a lantern, not a wall.

Years later, a student asks whether the Esho Current was a triumph or a mistake.

The instructor smiles.

"Open the map," she says.

insets.text: CIVIC MODULE STATUS: LAYERED  —  SOURCE CHAIN PUBLIC  —  ROUTE STEWARDSHIP RENEWED

overlays.text: The route is not the inheritance. The responsibility is.
The map stays open.

ending_silent_archive.text:
You seal the restricted archive.

Officially, the decision is temporary. A cooling period. A chance for education officers to review context, sequencing, civic readiness, and fourteen other beautiful names for fear.

The convoy remains calm.

The Esho story remains useful.

Years later, a child asks whether Elian Vale knew the route would work. The instructor smiles and gives the approved answer.

Behind three sealed doors, the fuller answer waits without aging.

That is the mercy and the crime of archives.

insets.text: RESTRICTED CHAIN SEALED  —  ACCESS: ASSEMBLY AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED

overlays.text: A truth can survive being buried. That does not mean burial is preservation.
